clue.text: Precocious players in second fiddle part

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for second

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it

indicators.note: to fiddle with something is to tamper with it, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gifted young musicians are stuck playing the supporting violin line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second fiddle' is not one phrase: 'fiddle' is the anagram signal, making RATP, and 'second' is a verb. The Brat Pack was a group of young Hollywood actors of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname was given to a set of young film actors who found fame early, players being actors.

clue.text: Vehicle propulsion reduced in joint

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: reduced means the word is made shorter by losing its last letter

parts.note: a push is an act of propulsion

explanation.surface: A car's driving force has been cut back at a coupling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' takes the final H off PUSH. The surface suggests a mechanical coupling; the definition is anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the anatomical name for the wrist, an example of a bodily hinge.

clue.text: To maybe make a handful of pieces, crushing one egg? One starts here

indicators.note: crushing means the phrase closes tightly around the other letters

parts.words: To maybe make a handful of pieces
parts.note: a handful is five, so to make five pieces of something is to split in five
one is I as a Roman numeral
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily breaks an egg while trying to divide something into a few bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushing' puts I NIT inside SPLIT IN FIVE. The clue opens with 'To maybe make', which is itself an example of the answer: hence 'One starts here'.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's opening words put an adverb between 'to' and its verb, a self-referential example of this grammatical construction.

clue.text: One bishop of a country wanting leadership could be pi

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and the leadership of a word is its first letter

parts.note: national means of a country

explanation.surface: A lone bishop from a leaderless land might be sanctimonious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting leadership' removes the first letter N from NATIONAL. 'pi' reads as slang for pious, but it is the mathematical constant, which cannot be written as a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The number pi is the best-known example of a number not expressible as a ratio of integers.

clue.text: Stone work's finish

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight (14 pounds)
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: The final surface treatment on a piece of masonry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to cease or bring to an end.

clue.text: Tailless primate connected to humans with asymmetry

indicators.note: tailless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a gibbon is a primate, an ape
we humans are us

explanation.surface: An ape with no tail is related to people, though lopsided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' drops the final N of GIBBON; 'connected to' simply joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: It describes the humped moon phase between half and full, bulging unevenly on one side.

clue.text: King Arthur's adviser half-flipped in seat of power

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

indicators.note: half-flipped means only one half of the wizard's name is turned back to front, the rest staying put

parts.note: Merlin was the wizard who counselled King Arthur

explanation.surface: The legendary king's wizard is partly overturned at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Arthur' splits in two: King alone gives one letter, and 'half-flipped' turns only the first three letters of the wizard's name, making REM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moscow citadel is the home of the Russian government, an example of a centre of rule.

clue.text: Necking second, drink to 13, 13 for a time?

indicators.note: necking is swallowing, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: to sup is to drink
the answer at 13 across is STOP, and to stop is to end

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink in a moment and counts thirteens.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 13s point to the answer at 13 across: the first supplies a synonym of it, the second with 'for a time' is the definition. 'Necking' is slang for swallowing, the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt something temporarily, with the intention of resuming later.

clue.text: After operation, pump iron, turning back on most of wreckage

indicators.note: on in an across clue means added at the end of the other part
most of means all but the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: debris is wreckage

indicators.note: turning back means the symbol is written right to left

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A patient recovering from surgery lifts weights with their back to a pile of rubble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the S of DEBRIS and 'turning back' makes FE into EF. 'pump iron' looks like weightlifting; 'pump' alone means to question closely, and the operation is a military one.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone closely for information once a mission is over.

clue.text: Offensive bit of Sun had to be read out

indicators.note: read out means the phrase is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a bit of sun is a ray, and ray had contracts to ray'd

explanation.surface: A distasteful item in the Sun newspaper had to be recited.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, and 'Offensive' looks like an adjective; it is a noun, a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are nouns for a military attack.

clue.text: Constant sound of impact in less impressive but versatile tool

parts.note: c is the abbreviation for a constant in mathematics and physics

indicators.note: in places the noise inside the comparative word

parts.note: lame means feeble, so lamer is less impressive
wham is the noise of a heavy blow

explanation.surface: A steady thumping comes from a modest but handy implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constant' reads as an adjective for the noise but is the scientific abbreviation; 'but' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It both drives nails and pulls them out, an example of an implement with more than one use.

clue.text: What's expected of aide, going forward, in emergency action?

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant

indicators.note: in places the adverb inside the word for emergency action

parts.note: recourse is something turned to for help in difficulty
forth means onward or forward

explanation.surface: What an assistant should do henceforth when a crisis strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going forward' reads as business jargon for 'from now on' but gives a plain adverb, and 'aide' is a personal assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfing idiom for the normal, anticipated result.

clue.text: Part of schemer gets to become known

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A plotter's role eventually comes to light.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: facts come out into the open.

clue.text: Pioneer of antisepsis breaks through with effects of chafing or burns?

definitions.text: with effects of chafing or burns?

indicators.note: breaks means the surgeon's name splits the short word and sits inside it

parts.note: by means through, as in 'by hard work'
Joseph Lister was the British surgeon who introduced antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: A medical innovator makes headway on sores and scalds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks through' looks like one phrase but splits: 'breaks' is the container signal and 'through' gives a two-letter preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective describing skin raised in fluid-filled bubbles from rubbing or heat.

clue.text: Suddenly overtakes runner taking it easy

indicators.note: overtakes here means one word takes the other over, enclosing it

parts.note: bang as an adverb means abruptly
a ski is a runner that slides over snow

explanation.surface: An athlete in a race coasts along after an abrupt burst past a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The runner is not an athlete but a blade for gliding on snow, and 'overtakes' is read as 'takes over', the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying relaxed in warmth or sunshine is one way of lazing.

clue.text: With nothing to lose, bunking off? That may be useful to hide work

definitions.text: That may be useful to hide work

indicators.note: nothing is the letter O, and to lose it means it is removed

parts.note: bunking off is British slang for playing truant, being absent without leave

explanation.surface: A truant with nothing at stake finds a way to conceal their homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With nothing to lose' removes O from AWOL. 'hide' is leather, not concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a pointed tool for piercing holes in leather.

clue.text: Protected by first bishop in Rome, I pitched into supplicant

indicators.note: protected by means the letters are sheltered inside the saint's name

parts.note: St Peter is traditionally regarded as the first Bishop of Rome

indicators.note: pitched means thrown, so the letters of the next word are tossed about

explanation.surface: Sheltered by the Pope, I threw myself at a beggar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitched' makes TION, which follows the I as written; 'Protected by' is the container signal. St Peter, not a pope by name, is the bishop meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms for one who makes a humble request.

clue.text: Equatorial country's argument against game

parts.note: a con is a point against, as in pros and cons
Go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A tropical nation makes its case for banning a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator runs through this African state.

clue.text: A recording showing passion

parts.note: vid is short for video

explanation.surface: A tape that reveals strong feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym for keenly enthusiastic.

clue.text: Post Office concerned with trademark admits trouble consists of dotty representation

parts.note: in can mean engaged in or concerned with, as in 'she is in insurance'

indicators.note: admits means the abbreviation lets the other letters inside

parts.note: ill means harm or trouble, as in 'to wish someone ill'
consists of can be replaced by is, as in 'the task is three parts'

explanation.surface: The Post Office, fretting over its logo, concedes that the problem is a crazy depiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dotty' reads as crazy but is literal: made of dots. 'admits' is the container signal, and 'consists of' is one piece, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Seurat's painting technique builds images from tiny spots of colour.

clue.text: Increase slope of line emitted by instrument with metal nib?

indicators.note: emitted by means the letter is given out, leaving the phrase

parts.note: a steel pen is a writing tool with a metal nib

explanation.surface: The stroke drawn by a fountain pen gets a sharper incline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emitted by' removes L from STEEL PEN. 'of' joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a gradient sharper.

clue.text: Cloaked outside of short coat taken on a journey

indicators.note: outside of means the first word goes round the other

parts.note: to cloak is to hide, so cloaked is hid

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a jacket is a short coat

explanation.surface: Someone wrapped up over a little jacket was brought along on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' means seized, not brought along. 'short' drops the coat's last letter, leaving JACKE, and 'outside of' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle seized by force in transit.

clue.text: Rip off before Observer intercepts once-powerful Frenchman

parts.note: to rip off is to rob

indicators.note: intercepts means the watcher cuts into the other word

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
a spier is one who spies or watches

explanation.surface: A scam is stopped by a newspaper before it reaches a former French bigwig.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, but here just someone who watches; 'intercepts' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the Reign of Terror in the French Revolution before his own execution.

clue.text: "Oban Summer" flops as a film

indicators.note: flops means falls about loosely, so the letters of the quoted title are rearranged

explanation.surface: A movie about a Scottish seaside holiday fails at the box office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flops' rearranges OBAN SUMMER. Oban is a Scottish resort town; the film is a thin skin, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective meaning like a thin skin or layer.

clue.text: Brotherhood — weird lot, I'd say

indicators.note: weird means strange, so the letters after it are put in an odd order

parts.note: the letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A fraternity is a strange bunch, in the speaker's opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' rearranges LOT, ID and SAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym for a fellowship or fraternity, especially a religious one.

clue.text: Mass removed from concertina after small hesitation

indicators.note: after says the trimmed word follows the abbreviation
removed from means the letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: to concertina is to crumple, folding up like the instrument
m is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A church service is dropped from a squeezebox recital after a brief pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' takes M out of CRUMPLE. 'concertina' is a verb here, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualm of conscience that makes one pause.

clue.text: Disregard attempt to eject teetotaller as fake

indicators.note: to eject means the abbreviation is thrown out of the joined words

parts.note: to forget something is to disregard it
a try is an attempt
TT is the abbreviation for teetotal or teetotaller

explanation.surface: Ignore the bid to throw out a non-drinker as an impostor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eject' removes TT from where FORGET meets TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are nouns for a counterfeit.

clue.text: I'm thrilled with large revolver

parts.note: whee is a cry of delight
L is the abbreviation for large on clothing

explanation.surface: A gun enthusiast is delighted with a big pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: The revolver is not a gun but simply a thing that revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a thing that turns round an axle.

clue.text: Hum quietly for musical number's introduction

indicators.note: for, with introduction, means one letter stands in place of the first letter of the next word

parts.note: a song is a musical number
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Softly croon the opening bars of a show tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quietly for ... introduction' replaces the first letter S of SONG with P. 'Hum' is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a stink.

clue.text: Country gentleman's whisky and port

definitions.meaning: a Romany word for a gentleman
an American whiskey made from this grain
one of the Cinque Ports, an old harbour town in Sussex, England

explanation.surface: A squire's spirits and fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gypsy word for a squire, a grain spirit and a Sussex harbour town share this spelling.
